page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, mapped to 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the CPU includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 640 GB NVMe SSD for local storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 10% and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, as well as Passmark memory scores, consistently align with average performance tiers.

Tradeoffs are evident in specialized workloads. While text processing benchmarks are strong, database operations and static web serving throughput fall into the weak category. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and LLM inference speeds for medium-sized 7B models show weak to poor performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides solid resource density for memory-intensive applications that do not require heavy multi-threaded compute. Appropriate workloads include memory-bound tasks, moderate software compilation, text processing, and general-purpose applications.
